description: Locked academic terminology from the human-authored manuscript. Machine-proposed rewrites must preserve these terms unless explicitly approved by a human moderator.

rules.rationale: 'Capabilities' is an established technical term in AI evaluation distinguishing what a system can do from what it tends to do; replacing it with 'abilities' dilutes precision and overrides human author terminology.
'Propensities' is the intentional technical term in the manuscript for behavioral dispositions under deployment; replacing it with 'tendencies' introduces machine-chosen terminology drift.

rules.paper_context: Taxonomy Tier 2 (Categories -> Open Problems -> Specific Challenges)
rules.rationale: Maintain strict 3-layer naming: Tier 1 = Categories (7), Tier 2 = Open Problems (30-50, synced with paper), Tier 3 = Specific Challenges / Questions (100s).
Construct validity captures whether an evaluation actually measures the intended property, distinct from mere statistical accuracy.
'Sociotechnical' denotes coupled human-AI-institutional systems rather than separable social and technical parts.
